display_name: Penfolds Bin 2 Mataro, South Eastern Australia
raw_content:
{
  "hook": "Bin 2 stands as the entry point into Penfolds' numbered Bin system, relying on old bush vine Mataro to temper Shiraz power. Warm McLaren Vale soils drive the jammy fruit profile, while the 14.5% ABV signals a ripe vintage style across the 2007-2013 run.",
  "wine_summary": "Across the 2007-2013 vintages, this label defined the Australian Shiraz-Mataro blend before the category had a name. Sourcing fruit from McLaren Vale's red-brown earths and dark cracking clays gives the wine dense plum flavors and a chewy texture. Penfolds maintains a house style through multi-vintage blending logic, ensuring consistency despite variable rainfall in the Fleurieu Zone.",
  "terroir_expression": "Driven by McLaren Vale's proximity to Gulf St Vincent, moderate heat allows the Mataro component to retain acidity despite the 14.5% alcohol. Rotundone compounds from the warm climate express as black pepper notes against the blackberry and licorice base. Elevations between 50 and 350 meters provide enough slope variation to avoid flabby textures in the final blend.",
  "vinification_summary": "Fermentation occurs in concrete and stainless steel to preserve primary fruit before aging in a mix of old and new American oak. The use of batch blending allows winemakers to combine parcels from different vineyards to meet a specific flavor target rather than expressing a single site. This approach prioritizes brand consistency over vintage variation, smoothing out tannins before bottling.",
  "food_pairing": "Pair smoked brisket sandwiches where fat cuts through the ripe tannins; try lamb moussaka since Mataro's savory edge matches the spiced meat; serve Nashville hot chicken because sweetness balances the heat and alcohol; match beef rendang as dark fruit stands up to coconut milk and spice; offer hard aged cheddar where salt contrasts the jammy berry flavors.",
  "comparable_wines": "For similar warm climate fruit, try Yalumba Old Bush Vine Grenache with bush vine sourcing; d'Arenberg The Dead Arm Shiraz shares McLaren Vale origin with concentrated dark fruit; Torbreck RunRig blends Shiraz with Rhône varieties for savory depth.",
  "style_profile": "Full-bodied dry red with soft tannins and jammy dark fruit.",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Aging beyond five years risks losing fruit sweetness, as the structure does not support long-term storage. Store upright in a cool dark place if consuming within a year, otherwise lay flat.",
  "value_assessment": "$25 to $35 places this above entry-level supermarket wines but below premium collectibles. Competitors like Wolf Blass Gold Label offer similar weight at a lower cost, while Two Hands Bella's Garden commands a higher price for single-region focus. The Bin 2 price reflects the brand tax rather than superior vineyard sourcing.",
  "market_position": "On restaurant lists, this bottle features for diners seeking recognizable Australian names without Grange prices. Retail shelves position it as a step-up gift option for customers familiar with the Penfolds logo. Collectors ignore this label in favor of Bin 389 or 707, leaving it to casual drinkers wanting reliability.",
  "insider_take": "Do not buy this bottle if you want terroir transparency, as blending obscures specific vineyard character. Purchase when you need a reliable crowd-pleaser that won't challenge palates accustomed to New World fruit. The tradeoff is personality for consistency, which suits large dinner parties but not serious tasting.",
  "aging_potential_years": 5,

  }
}
